docs.title: PRISM Capability
docs.text: Part of the PRISM ecosystem. Defines capability stacks with layers, capabilities, and maturity integration.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PRISM Capability defines what capabilities exist in an organization's technology landscape. It integrates with prism-intelligence to track maturity levels and prism-roadmap for improvement roadmaps.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       prism-capability                              │
│              "These are the capabilities we need"                   │
│         Layers, capabilities, categories, relationships             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              │ references
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      prism-intelligence                             │
│         Maturity models, SLIs/SLOs, state tracking                  │
│  "What does M4 look like?" + "Capability X is at M2"                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              │ references
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       prism-roadmap                                 │
│              OKRs, roadmaps, improvement initiatives                │
│       "Move SAST from M2→M4 by Q3 via these initiatives"            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Capability Stack Definition: JSON-based specification for organizational capabilities
  • Layered Architecture: Organize capabilities by technology layer (infrastructure, platform, application)
  • Priority Framework: Tier capabilities by business criticality (Existential, Critical, Strategic, Enhancement)
  • Dynamic Priority: Calculate P0-P3 priorities from importance weights and maturity gaps
  • Validation: Comprehensive validation with dependency cycle detection
  • Rendering: Generate D2 diagrams, static HTML, and interactive Lit web components
  • Overlays: External modules can inject display data (badges, tooltips) into renderers

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install CLI
go install github.com/grokify/prism-capability/cmd/capstack@latest

# Validate a capability stack
capstack validate my-stack.json

# Render as HTML
capstack render my-stack.json --format html --output stack.html

# List capabilities filtered by status
capstack list my-stack.json --status operational

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Full API documentation is available at pkg.go.dev.

docs.title: CapabilityStack
docs.text:
The root document type:

type CapabilityStack struct {
    Metadata          Metadata
    Layers            []Layer
    Categories        []Category
    Capabilities      []Capability
    Foundational      []Capability
    PriorityFramework *PriorityFramework
    MarketIntegration *MarketIntegration
}

Key methods:

// Load from file
cs, err := capstack.LoadFromFile("stack.json")

// Validate
errs := cs.Validate()

// Query capabilities
byStatus := cs.CapabilitiesByStatus(capstack.StatusOperational)
byLayer := cs.CapabilitiesByLayer("application")
byCategory := cs.CapabilitiesByCategory("security")
all := cs.AllCapabilities()

// Sort
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByImportance)
sorted := cs.SortedCapabilities(capstack.SortByOrder)

docs.title: Capability
docs.text:
type Capability struct {
    ID           string
    Name         string
    Description  string
    LayerID      string
    CategoryID   string
    Status       string
    Priority     string
    Importance   string
    Order        int
    TargetDate   string
    Owner        string
    Tags         []string
    Dependencies []string
    PRISMRef     *PRISMRef
    MarketRef    *MarketRef
}

docs.title: Priority Functions
docs.text:
// Get importance weight (4=critical, 3=high, 2=medium, 1=low)
weight := capstack.ImportanceWeight("critical") // 4

// Calculate dynamic priority (P0-P3)
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("critical", 1, 3) // "P0"

// Get priority weight
weight := capstack.DynamicPriorityWeight("P0") // 4

docs.title: capstack list
docs.text: List capabilities with optional filtering.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: capstack list <file> [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Description --status Filter by status (planned, in-progress, implemented, operational, deprecated) --layer Filter by layer ID --tag Filter by tag

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:

capstack list my-stack.json

# Filter by status
capstack list my-stack.json --status operational

# Filter by layer
capstack list my-stack.json --layer application

# Combine filters
capstack list my-stack.json --status implemented --layer platform

docs.title: capstack render
docs.text: Generate visualizations from a capability stack.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: capstack render <file> [flags]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Description Default --format, -f Output format: d2, html, lit, or json d2 --output, -o Output file path stdout --standalone Include full HTML document true --dark Use dark theme (HTML/lit) false --legend Show status legend/filters true --style D2 style: default or grid default --view View mode: by-layer or by-category (lit/json) by-layer --component-path Path to prism-ui.js component (lit) prism-ui.js

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# HTML output to file
capstack render my-stack.json --format html -o stack.html

# HTML fragment (embeddable)
capstack render my-stack.json --format html --standalone=false

# Dark theme
capstack render my-stack.json --format html --dark -o stack-dark.html

# D2 diagram
capstack render my-stack.json --format d2 -o stack.d2

# D2 grid style (executive view)
capstack render my-stack.json --format d2 --style grid -o stack-grid.d2

# Convert D2 to SVG (requires d2 installed)
d2 stack.d2 stack.svg

# Lit web component (interactive)
capstack render my-stack.json --format lit -o stack.html

# Lit with category view and dark theme
capstack render my-stack.json --format lit --view by-category --dark -o stack.html

# JSON data for custom integration
capstack render my-stack.json --format json -o stack-data.json

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
The JSON renderer outputs structured data for custom Lit component integration:

  • layers: Layer definitions with IDs and names
  • categories: Category definitions
  • capabilities: Capability data with layer/category associations
  • maturity: Optional maturity level data

Use JSON output when integrating with custom web applications or when you need programmatic access to the rendered data structure.

docs.title: capstack validate
docs.text: Validate a capability stack document.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: capstack validate <file>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Validates the structure and content of a capability stack JSON file, checking:

  • Required fields (id, name, layerId for capabilities)
  • Kebab-case ID format
  • Valid enum values (status, priority, domain)
  • Reference integrity (layerId, categoryId exist)
  • Dependency cycle detection
  • Order uniqueness (if any non-zero Order)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Validate a document
capstack validate my-stack.json

# Valid output
Valid: my-stack.json
  Name: my-org-capabilities
  Version: 1.0.0
  Domain: operations
  Layers: 7
  Categories: 6
  Capabilities: 26
  Foundational: 3

# Invalid output
Invalid: my-stack.json
Errors:
  - capabilities[5].layerId: references non-existent layer "missing-layer"
  - capabilities[8].order: duplicate order value, also used by capability[2]

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Valid document 1 Validation errors found

docs.title: Greenfield Workflow
docs.text:
When building a new system, most capabilities start as planned:

Month 1-2: Define capability stack
├── All capabilities marked "planned"
├── Dependencies identified
├── Priorities set (critical → high → medium → low)
└── Target dates assigned

Month 3-6: Foundation phase
├── Critical capabilities → in-progress → implemented
├── PRISM state created for implemented capabilities
├── Baseline measurements captured (M1-M2)
└── High-priority capabilities started

Month 6-12: Build-out phase
├── High/medium capabilities → implemented
├── Critical capabilities → operational (M3-M4)
├── PRISM plan tracks maturity improvements
└── Gap analysis drives prioritization

Year 2+: Optimization phase
├── All core capabilities operational
├── Focus on M4 → M5 maturity
├── New capabilities added as needed
└── Continuous improvement culture

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text: Overlays allow external modules to inject supplemental display data into capability renderers without tight coupling.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The overlay system enables:

  • Maturity badges: Show M1-M5 levels on capabilities
  • Custom tooltips: Add context from external data sources
  • Color coding: Highlight capabilities based on external state

docs.title: CapabilityOverlay
docs.text:
type CapabilityOverlay struct {
    // BadgeText is displayed as a badge (e.g., "M3", "L2")
    BadgeText string

    // BadgeColor is the background color (e.g., "#22c55e")
    BadgeColor string

    // BadgeTextColor is the text color
    BadgeTextColor string

    // TooltipExtra is appended to the capability tooltip
    TooltipExtra string
}

docs.title: OverlayProvider
docs.text:
Map capability IDs to their overlays:

overlays := render.OverlayProvider{
    "sast": {
        BadgeText:    "M3",
        BadgeColor:   "#22c55e",
        TooltipExtra: "Target: M4 by Q3",
    },
    "dast": {
        BadgeText:    "M1",
        BadgeColor:   "#ef4444",
        TooltipExtra: "Critical gap - immediate action",
    },
    "logging": {
        BadgeText:    "M4",
        BadgeColor:   "#3b82f6",
        TooltipExtra: "Meeting SLOs",
    },
}

docs.title: Integration with prism-maturity
docs.text:
The primary use case is integrating maturity state from prism-maturity:

import (
    capstack "github.com/grokify/prism-capability"
    "github.com/grokify/prism-capability/render"
    "github.com/grokify/prism-maturity/dashboard"
)

// Load capability stack and maturity state
cs, _ := capstack.LoadFromFile("stack.json")
state, _ := dashboard.LoadState("state.json")

// Build overlays from maturity state
overlays := make(render.OverlayProvider)
for _, cap := range cs.AllCapabilities() {
    if sliIDs := cap.PRISMRef.SliIDs; len(sliIDs) > 0 {
        level := state.GetAggregateLevel(sliIDs)
        overlays[cap.ID] = render.CapabilityOverlay{
            BadgeText:  fmt.Sprintf("M%d", level),
            BadgeColor: dashboard.MaturityColor(level),
        }
    }
}

// Render with overlays
opts := render.DefaultHTMLOptions()
opts.Overlays = overlays
html, _ := render.RenderHTMLString(cs, opts)

docs.title: Default Badge Colors
docs.text:
If BadgeColor is not specified:

  • Badge text starting with "M" gets indigo (#6366f1)
  • Other badges get slate gray (#64748b)
  • BadgeTextColor defaults to white (#ffffff)

docs.title: Priority Framework
docs.text: The priority framework helps organize capabilities by business criticality and calculate dynamic priorities based on maturity gaps.

docs.title: Importance Levels
docs.text:
Static importance weights for capabilities, layers, and categories:

Level Weight Description critical 4 Essential "-ilities" (security, availability, compliance) high 3 High business impact capabilities medium 2 Standard importance (default) low 1 Nice-to-have capabilities 
{
  "id": "sast",
  "name": "SAST",
  "importance": "critical",
  "order": 1
}

docs.title: Capability Ordering
docs.text:
Explicit ordering for consistent display and tier assignment:

{
  "capabilities": [
    {"id": "sast", "name": "SAST", "order": 1},
    {"id": "dast", "name": "DAST", "order": 2},
    {"id": "sca", "name": "SCA", "order": 3}
  ]
}

Validation rules:

  • If any capability has a non-zero Order, all Order values must be unique
  • Capabilities with Order=0 are sorted after those with explicit ordering

docs.title: Dynamic Priority (P0-P3)
docs.text:
Calculate dynamic priority from importance and maturity gap:

Priority Score = Importance Weight × (Target Level - Current Level)
Score Priority Action ≥8 P0 Immediate action required ≥4 P1 High priority improvement ≥2 P2 Scheduled improvement <2 P3 Low priority enhancement

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
// Critical capability (weight=4) at M1 with target M3:
// Score = 4 × 2 = 8 → P0
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("critical", 1, 3)

// Medium capability (weight=2) at M2 with target M3:
// Score = 2 × 1 = 2 → P2
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("medium", 2, 3)

// Already at target: P3
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("critical", 3, 3)

docs.title: Querying by Tier
docs.text:
pf := cs.PriorityFramework

// Get tier for a capability

docs.title: Sorting Methods
docs.text:
Sort capabilities by different criteria:

// By explicit Order field (default)
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByOrder)

// Alphabetically by name
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByName)

// By importance weight (critical first)
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByImportance)

// By static priority field
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByPriority)

// By lifecycle status (operational first)
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByStatus)

// Get sorted copy without modifying original
sorted := cs.SortedCapabilities(capstack.SortByImportance)

docs.title: Create a Capability Stack
docs.text:
Create a new capability stack document:

capstack init my-stack.json

Or create one manually:

{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grokify/prism-capability/main/schema/capstack.schema.json",
  "metadata": {
    "id": "my-org-capabilities",
    "name": "my-org-capabilities",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "title": "My Organization Capabilities"
  },
  "layers": [
    {"id": "infrastructure", "name": "Infrastructure", "order": 1},
    {"id": "platform", "name": "Platform", "order": 2},
    {"id": "application", "name": "Application", "order": 3}
  ],
  "categories": [
    {"id": "security", "name": "Security", "color": "#ef4444"},
    {"id": "observability", "name": "Observability", "color": "#3b82f6"}
  ],
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "id": "sast",
      "name": "SAST",
      "layerId": "application",
      "categoryId": "security",
      "status": "implemented",
      "importance": "critical",
      "order": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "logging",
      "name": "Centralized Logging",
      "layerId": "platform",
      "categoryId": "observability",
      "status": "operational",
      "importance": "high",
      "order": 10
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
capstack validate my-stack.json

Output:

Valid: my-stack.json
  Name: my-org-capabilities
  Version: 1.0.0
  Layers: 3
  Categories: 2
  Capabilities: 2

docs.title: List Capabilities
docs.text:
# List all
capstack list my-stack.json

# Filter by status
capstack list my-stack.json --status operational

# Filter by layer
capstack list my-stack.json --layer application

docs.title: Render Visualizations
docs.text:
# Lit web component (interactive, recommended)
capstack render my-stack.json --format lit --output stack.html

# Lit with dark theme and category view
capstack render my-stack.json --format lit --dark --view by-category --output stack.html

# Static HTML
capstack render my-stack.json --format html --output stack.html

# D2 diagram
capstack render my-stack.json --format d2 --output stack.d2
d2 stack.d2 stack.svg

# JSON data for custom integration
capstack render my-stack.json --format json --output stack-data.json

docs.title: Use as Library
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"

    capstack "github.com/grokify/prism-capability"
    "github.com/grokify/prism-capability/render"
)

func main() {
    // Load capability stack
    cs, err := capstack.LoadFromFile("my-stack.json")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Validate
    errs := cs.Validate()
    if len(errs) > 0 {
        log.Fatal(errs)
    }

    // Query capabilities
    operational := cs.CapabilitiesByStatus(capstack.StatusOperational)
    fmt.Printf("Operational: %d capabilities\n", len(operational))

    // Sort by importance
    cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByImportance)

    // Render HTML
    html, _ := render.RenderHTMLString(cs, render.DefaultHTMLOptions())
    fmt.Println(html)
}

docs.title: v0.1.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-05-17

Initial release of capability-stack-spec, a Go library and CLI for defining capability stacks with layers, capabilities, and PRISM maturity integration.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Go Types & Validation: Complete type system matching JSON Schema with comprehensive validation including reference integrity and dependency cycle detection
  • CLI Tool: capstack command with validate, init, list, show, and render commands
  • Diagram Rendering: D2 diagrams (default and executive grid styles) and static HTML output
  • Web Component: Lit-based <capability-stack> element for embedding in websites and MkDocs

docs.title: Core Types
docs.text: Type Purpose CapabilityStack Root document with metadata, layers, categories, capabilities Capability Individual capability with lifecycle status, dependencies, tooling Layer Horizontal band representing phases or stages Category Visual grouping with optional color Tool Tooling information with vendor, type, status PRISMRef Reference to PRISM maturity model for SLI tracking

docs.title: Enum Constants
docs.text:
• CapabilityStatus: planned, in-progress, implemented, operational, deprecated
  • Priority: critical, high, medium, low
  • Domain: security, ai, platform, data, observability, infrastructure, product, operations
  • Phase: plan, design, build, test, release, deploy, operate, monitor, respond, recover
  • Framework: nist-csf-2.0, nist-800-53, iso-27001, soc2, pci-dss, cis, mitre-attack, owasp, slsa, ssdf

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text:
# Validate a capability stack document
capstack validate stack.json

# Create a new capability stack
capstack init -d security -o security-stack.json

# List capabilities with filtering
capstack list stack.json --status=implemented --layer=build-test

# Show capability details
capstack show stack.json sast

# Render to D2 diagram
capstack render stack.json -o stack.d2
capstack render stack.json --style=grid -o exec-view.d2

# Render to HTML
capstack render stack.json -f html --standalone -o stack.html

docs.title: Validation Features
docs.text:
• Required fields: id, name, layerId for capabilities
  • Kebab-case ID format enforcement
  • Enum value validation for all constants
  • Reference integrity (layerId, categoryId must exist)
  • Unique ID enforcement across layers, categories, capabilities
  • Dependency cycle detection using DFS

docs.title: D2 Diagram Styles
docs.text: Style Description default Standard view with dependency arrows grid Clean executive view - aligned boxes, no arrows, shadows

docs.title: HTML Options
docs.text: Flag Description --standalone Generate complete HTML document --dark Use dark color theme --no-legend Hide status legend --no-foundational Hide foundational capabilities

docs.title: Web Component
docs.text:
<script type="module" src="capability-stack.js"></script>

<capability-stack
  src="stack.json"
  theme="light"
  show-legend
  show-foundational
  interactive>
</capability-stack>

Works with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs (unlike React components).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• examples/operations-saas-greenfield.json - SRE/Operations reference architecture
  • examples/security-saas-greenfield.json - B2B SaaS security stack

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# CLI
go install github.com/grokify/prism-capability/cmd/capstack@latest

# Library
go get github.com/grokify/prism-capability

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text:
This release establishes the foundation for the PRISM ecosystem:

  • prism-capability (this project) - What capabilities exist
  • prism-intelligence - Maturity models, SLIs/SLOs, state tracking
  • prism-execution - OKRs, roadmaps, improvement initiatives

The repository has been renamed to github.com/grokify/prism-capability as of v0.2.0.

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text:
1. Update go.mod to use the new module path
  2. Run go mod tidy to update dependencies
  3. Update all import statements in your code
  4. The API remains unchanged - only the import paths have changed

docs.title: v0.3.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-05-18

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Market Integration: New MarketRef type for linking organizational capabilities to market capabilities from market-strategy-engine
  • PRISM Core Integration: Types now imported from prism-core v0.1.0

docs.title: MarketRef Type
docs.text:
Capabilities can now reference market capabilities for strategic alignment:

{
  "id": "sast",
  "name": "SAST",
  "marketRef": {
    "marketId": "enterprise-security",
    "capabilityIds": ["secure-sdlc", "compliance-automation"],
    "segments": ["enterprise", "regulated"],
    "impact": "high",
    "gapContribution": [
      {
        "capabilityId": "secure-sdlc",
        "segmentId": "regulated",
        "contribution": "primary",
        "description": "Enables shift-left security for regulated industries"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: MarketIntegration Configuration
docs.text:
Global market integration settings at the document level:

{
  "marketIntegration": {
    "analysisRef": "market-analysis-2026-q2.json",
    "defaultMarket": "enterprise-security",
    "focusSegments": ["enterprise", "mid-market"]
  }
}

docs.title: New Query Methods
docs.text:
• CapabilitiesByMarketCapability(marketCapID) - Find org capabilities that enable a market capability
  • CapabilitiesByMarket(marketID) - Find org capabilities linked to a specific market
  • CapabilitiesForSegment(segmentID) - Find org capabilities that benefit a market segment

docs.title: prism-core Integration
docs.text:
The following types are now imported from github.com/grokify/prism-core instead of being defined locally:

Type Package Priority prism-core Domain prism-core NIST CSF functions prism-core

This ensures consistency across the PRISM ecosystem.

docs.text:

docs.title: v0.4.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-05-24

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Importance & Priority: Static importance weights with dynamic P0-P3 priority calculation based on maturity gaps
  • Priority Framework: Organize capabilities into tiered groups (Existential/Critical/Strategic/Enhancement)
  • Overlay System: External modules can inject display data (badges, tooltips) into renderers
  • Interactive HTML: Status and maturity filters with badge display

docs.title: Importance Field
docs.text:
Capabilities, layers, and categories now have an importance field for static weighting:

{
  "id": "sast",
  "name": "SAST",
  "importance": "critical",
  "order": 1
}
Level Weight Description critical 4 Essential "-ilities" (security, availability) high 3 High business impact medium 2 Standard importance (default) low 1 Nice-to-have

docs.title: Dynamic Priority (P0-P3)
docs.text:
Calculate dynamic priority from importance and maturity gap:

// Priority = Importance Weight × (Target Level - Current Level)
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("critical", 1, 3) // Returns "P0" (4 × 2 = 8)
priority := capstack.CalculatePriority("medium", 2, 3)   // Returns "P2" (2 × 1 = 2)
Score Priority Action ≥8 P0 Immediate action required ≥4 P1 High priority improvement ≥2 P2 Scheduled improvement <2 P3 Low priority enhancement

docs.title: Priority Framework
docs.text:
Organize capabilities into priority tiers:

{
  "priorityFramework": {
    "title": "Capability Priorities",
    "tiers": [
      {
        "id": "tier-1",
        "name": "Tier 1",
        "orderRange": {"min": 1, "max": 5},
        "orders": "Existential",
        "focus": ["Security", "Availability", "Compliance"]
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Capability Sorting
docs.text:
Multiple sort methods available:

cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByOrder)      // By explicit Order field
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByImportance) // By importance weight
cs.SortCapabilities(capstack.SortByStatus)     // By lifecycle status

// Get sorted copy
sorted := cs.SortedCapabilities(capstack.SortByName)

docs.title: Overlay Provider
docs.text:
External modules can inject display data:

overlays := render.OverlayProvider{
    "sast": {
        BadgeText:    "M3",
        BadgeColor:   "#22c55e",
        TooltipExtra: "Target: M4 by Q3",
    },
}

opts := render.DefaultD2Options()
opts.Overlays = overlays
render.RenderD2(doc, opts)

docs.title: Interactive HTML Filters
docs.text:
HTML output now includes:

  • Status filter checkboxes (Operational, Implemented, In Progress, Planned, Deprecated)
  • Maturity level filters (M1-M5) when overlays are present
  • Select All / Clear All buttons
  • Badge display for capabilities with overlay data

docs.title: CLI Package Extraction
docs.text:
CLI commands moved from cmd/capstack/ to reusable cli/ package:

// Embed in another CLI
import "github.com/grokify/prism-capability/cli"

rootCmd.AddCommand(cli.ValidateCmd)
rootCmd.AddCommand(cli.RenderCmd)

docs.title: v0.5.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-06-06

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Lit Web Component Rendering: Interactive HTML output with filtering, sorting, and view toggling
  • Priority Frameworks Integration: Standardized priority handling via priority-frameworks package

docs.title: Lit Web Component Output
docs.text:
New lit format generates interactive HTML with a modern Lit web component:

# Generate interactive Lit HTML
capstack render stack.json --format lit -o stack.html

# With dark theme and category view
capstack render stack.json --format lit --dark --view=by-category -o stack.html

Features:

  • View toggle between layer and category grouping
  • Interactive status filtering
  • Sorting options
  • Dark/light theme support
  • Responsive design

docs.title: JSON Data Output
docs.text:
New json format outputs structured data for custom Lit component integration:

capstack render stack.json --format json -o stack-data.json

Use this when building custom web applications or dashboards.

docs.title: CLI Flags
docs.text: Flag Description --view View mode: by-layer (default) or by-category --component-path Path to prism-ui.js component file

docs.title: Framework Accessor Functions
docs.text:
New functions expose priority frameworks for programmatic use:

import capstack "github.com/grokify/prism-capability"

// Get specific frameworks
severity := capstack.SeverityFramework()    // Critical/High/Medium/Low
priority := capstack.PriorityFrameworkP()   // P0/P1/P2/P3
moscow := capstack.MoSCoWFramework()        // Must/Should/Could/Won't
ietf := capstack.IETFFramework()            // MUST/SHOULD/MAY
general := capstack.GeneralFramework()      // Required/Recommended/Optional

// Get framework by ID
fw := capstack.GetFramework("severity")

docs.title: Operations Site Example
docs.text:
New example in examples/operations-site/ demonstrates Lit component integration:

  • index.html: Landing page with navigation
  • by-layer.html: Capabilities grouped by layer
  • by-category.html: Capabilities grouped by category
  • maturity.html: Maturity assessment view
  • metrics.html: Operations metrics dashboard

docs.title: Priority Frameworks Migration
docs.text:
Internal priority handling now uses the priority-frameworks package:

  • ImportanceWeight() uses pf.Severity() internally
  • DynamicPriorityWeight() uses pf.Priority() internally
  • ValidPriority() validates against SeverityFramework()

This provides consistent priority semantics across the PRISM ecosystem.

docs.title: v0.6.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-06-28

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Operations & DevOps Frameworks: Add DORA and SRE framework constants
  • Developer Productivity Frameworks: Add SPACE, AI-DORA, and AI-SPACE framework support
  • Developer Experience Metrics: Canonical SLI definitions for productivity measurement

docs.title: Framework Constants
docs.text:
New framework constants for operations and developer productivity:

import capstack "github.com/grokify/prism-capability"

// Operations & DevOps
capstack.FrameworkDORA  // DevOps Research and Assessment
capstack.FrameworkSRE   // Site Reliability Engineering

// Developer Productivity
capstack.FrameworkSPACE   // Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication, Efficiency
capstack.FrameworkAIDORA  // AI-Modified DORA
capstack.FrameworkAISPACE // AI-Modified SPACE

docs.title: Framework Helper Functions
docs.text:
New functions for querying framework categories:

// Get operations-focused frameworks
ops := capstack.OperationsFrameworks()
// Returns: ["dora", "sre", "ai-dora"]

// Get developer productivity frameworks
devprod := capstack.DeveloperProductivityFrameworks()
// Returns: ["space", "ai-space"]

// Get AI-enhanced frameworks
ai := capstack.AIFrameworks()
// Returns: ["ai-dora", "ai-space"]

docs.title: Developer Experience Metrics
docs.text:
New metrics/devex.json provides canonical SLI definitions:

  • DORA Metrics: Deployment frequency, lead time, MTTR, change failure rate
  • SPACE Metrics: Satisfaction, performance, activity, communication, efficiency dimensions
  • AI-DORA Metrics: AI-accelerated baselines for DORA metrics
  • AI-SPACE Metrics: 25 metrics across 5 dimensions for AI-enhanced productivity

Each metric includes:

  • Performance level thresholds (elite, high, medium, low)
  • Measurement units and direction (higher/lower is better)
  • Framework attribution and references
